trust_decision.summary: The client decides whether to send the password in plaintext when the server names the auth plugin mysql_clear_password. At the pinned commit it does so with no client opt-in, both in the auth-switch handler and in the initial-handshake direct-auth shortcut. The fix gates both on config.enableCleartextPlugin or on a custom authPlugins.mysql_clear_password entry.

landing_point.why: The summary says 'auth plugin downgrade'. A server-sent AuthSwitchRequest naming mysql_clear_password is resolved here through getAuthPlugin into the built-in cleartext plugin, so this is where an engineer would look first.

fix_sites.entry_point: mysql.createConnection()/createPool()/promise wrappers -> ClientHandshake.handshakeResult (lib/commands/client_handshake.js:338); also connection.changeUser() via lib/commands/change_user.js:63-64 and MFA AuthNextFactor (marker 0x02, lib/commands/client_handshake.js:319-338)
mysql.createConnection() with ssl or socketPath set: the initial HandshakeResponse direct-auth optimization (sendCredentials)
fix_sites.module_kind: second code path in another file (handshake optimization that bypasses auth switch)

fix_sites.entry_point: same as auth_switch: keeps the new error code instead of overwriting it with AUTH_SWITCH_PLUGIN_ERROR
ConnectionConfig constructor, used by createConnection, PoolConfig (lib/pool_config.js:8-10) and URI strings (lib/connection_config.js:272-293)

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: lib/commands/client_handshake.js:105-119 (direct-auth shortcut: canUseAuthMethodDirectly at :203-219 returns true for mysql_clear_password when ssl/socketPath is set, and calculateAuthToken at :189-194 builds the plaintext token without any plugin)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The direct-auth shortcut only fires when ssl or socketPath is configured (client_handshake.js:78-79, :210-213), so a solver can argue the channel is already secure and the report's 'downgrade' is only the AuthSwitchRequest path. The fix still requires opt-in there, because a malicious or impersonated server receives the plaintext password.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Cleartext auth must keep working when the user opts in (enableCleartextPlugin:true, or a custom authPlugins.mysql_clear_password, which the fix treats as implicit opt-in), including direct use over TLS/socket. Other plaintext-over-TLS plugins (sha256_password, caching_sha2 full auth) must keep working, and existing unit tests expect canUseAuthMethodDirectly('mysql_clear_password', true) === true. An over-broad fix that rejects the plugin outright, ignores custom authPlugins, or edits canUseAuthMethodDirectly breaks these.

O6_input_shapes: server AuthNextFactor (0x02, MFA) naming mysql_clear_password, through the same authSwitchRequest
server initial Handshake advertising mysql_clear_password as the default plugin, with ssl/socketPath configured (direct-auth path)
opt-in through an authPlugins own-property 'mysql_clear_password' (hasOwnProperty check)
option given through a URI query string or pool config (ConnectionConfig.parseUrl JSON-parses values)

O7_producer.where: lib/connection_config.js:74-194 (ConnectionConfig constructor; the option must be copied to this.enableCleartextPlugin at fix.diff:81, and the whitelist entry at fix.diff:73 only silences a warning)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: A legacy authSwitchHandler is invoked for a server-requested mysql_clear_password before the new gate. The fix leaves it ungated (the handler receives the pluginName and decides itself).
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: The handler is deprecated user-supplied code, and client_handshake already treats it as an explicit opt-out of built-in auth (client_handshake.js:100-101). This is a weak route that is probably intentional.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file as the landing point, 15 lines above

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Give ChangeUser its own auth-switch handling (a copy of handshakeResult/authSwitchRequest) that resolves plugins through standardAuthPlugins without the gate.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: ChangeUser already borrows ClientHandshake methods piecemeal. A maintainer handling re-auth separately (it resets currentConfig.password at :43) could plausibly have forked the logic.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Server-driven PERFORM_FULL_AUTHENTICATION sends the plaintext password whenever config.ssl/socketPath is truthy or overrideIsSecure is set, not when the stream is actually encrypted. Unlike sha256_password.js:42-48 it does not check the TLS socket.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: This is a real asymmetry between two plugins that do the same job. A planted variant without the isSecureConnection check would be a how-type sibling in a plugin module the report does not name.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: The uri merge skips only truthy explicit options, so enableCleartextPlugin:false plus uri '?enableCleartextPlugin=true' ends up enabled. A defaults/merge route for the opt-in flag.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: This is the existing merge idiom for every option, so a maintainer would not have special-cased a security flag.

O9_family: CWE-522 insufficiently protected credentials (client auth-plugin downgrade to cleartext, missing opt-in gate)

O10_build.toolchain: npm install; poku test runner (package.json:11); node >= 8 per package.json:51
O10_build.project_tests: The fix's test (test/integration/test-cleartext-plugin-gate.test.mts) uses an in-process mysql.createServer mock, so it needs no MySQL server. Existing unit tests are in test/unit/commands/test-client-handshake-auth.test.mts:186-200. Most other integration tests need a MySQL server (docker-compose), but hidden tests for this area can use the mock-server pattern.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Add an opt-in check only in authSwitchRequest (or in the mysql_clear_password plugin) and leave the client_handshake direct-auth shortcut sending plaintext whenever ssl/socketPath is set.

out_of_scope_notes: The server-side ConnectionConfig use in lib/server.js:18 is not part of the client auth decision and was not examined.

O8 has only a weak route (the legacy handler); other paths to the cleartext sink (changeUser, MFA AuthNextFactor) go through authSwitchRequest and are covered by the fix.
